tool.name: Claude Chat
tool.summary: The conversational Claude experience — for asking questions, drafting, analysing, summarising, translating and creating reusable outputs.

responsibilityNote: Claude can accelerate your work, but you remain responsible for what you enter, approve, share and publish. Follow Sandvik policy, protect sensitive information, and review outputs before relying on them.

courseStart.whatThisModuleAdds: The AI Fluency foundation covered the general rules of safe AI use — approved tools, protecting information, giving useful context, iterating, and checking confident answers. Here you apply that inside Claude Chat: what it does well, how its context features work, what Sandvik allows, and what to verify before you trust an answer.

foundation.label: AI Fluency
foundation.blurb: Safe AI use, prompting, responsible-AI principles, and the idea of agents.

assumedKnowledge: General rules of safe AI use: approved tools, protect information, give context, iterate, verify
The concept of agents: a role, instructions and data sources, built once and reused
journeyContext.thisModuleFocusesOn: Using Claude Chat day to day — and on agentic, tool-assisted chat: not a separate agent you build, but Claude working through multiple steps inside the conversation, using approved context and tools, and continuing from what it finds. Building and sharing your own agents is covered in the AI Champion Journey.
objectives: Use Claude Chat's features to get better context into your prompts.
Use files, connectors, projects, skills and artifacts responsibly where approved.
Manage usage and cost by scoping context, tool use and long conversations deliberately.
Verify and share outputs safely, with Sandvik policy and human accountability in mind.

toolFit.intro: Claude Chat holds the foundational features of Claude. It is not Claude Code, Cowork or Design. Choosing the right product is the first decision.
useWhen: You are thinking through a problem and want an interactive thought partner.
You need a first draft, summary, translation, comparison, checklist or structured analysis.
You want to upload or paste selected context and ask questions about it.
You want text or an artifact you can inspect, edit and reuse.
You want Claude to use approved tools or connectors inside a controlled conversation.

useOtherWhen.if: The deliverable spans many files, browser steps or desktop actions
You need to read and change a codebase, run tests or use dev tools
The main output is visual exploration, prototypes, slides or design

decisionTable.work: Conversational thinking, drafts, summaries, analysis, Q&A on context you provide
A deliverable across many files, the browser, or desktop actions
Reading and changing a codebase, running tests, using dev tools
Visual exploration, prototypes, slides, design concepts

steps.title: Prepare context
steps.body: Open a chat or project; add only material you're cleared to use.

steps.title: Set boundaries
steps.body: State role, format and limits. Say what's confidential.

steps.title: Use the tool
steps.body: Ask, iterate, refine with follow-ups — not one giant prompt.

steps.title: Review output
steps.body: Treat every answer as a draft. Verify facts and figures.

steps.title: Share safely
steps.body: Only paste into approved channels. Remove what shouldn't leave Sandvik.

agenticChat.blurb: Ask Claude to plan first. It can create a checklist and work through it item by item, adapting to your feedback — keeping track of progress inside the conversation.

toolAssistedFlow: You ask Claude for a daily summary from your emails.
Claude identifies that inbox context is needed.
It uses a Sandvik-approved email connector, via your permissions.
Claude drafts the summary from that context.
You review sources, assumptions and policy before sharing or acting.
coreWorkflow.accountabilityNote: You remain responsible for deciding whether the tool should be used, whether the context is appropriate, and whether the output is reliable enough to act on.

capabilities.intro: Each feature changes what Claude can see, retrieve, reuse or produce. Use them deliberately.

cards.title: Files
cards.body: Work with material you provide — reports, spreadsheets, notes, specs. Claude can summarise, compare, extract, rewrite and answer questions about the content.
cards.note: Watch: more context isn't always better. For data, verify calculations against the source.

cards.title: Connectors
cards.body: Approved apps and services bring extra context into a chat. Claude works through your login and permissions — M365 (pending approval), HubSpot, GitHub.
cards.note: Watch: prefer narrow access; pause before any write action; watch for prompt injection in retrieved content.

cards.title: Projects
cards.body: Focused workspaces with their own chats, project knowledge and instructions. Upload approved materials once; set stable tone and terminology.
cards.note: Check: who can access it, whether they may see the knowledge, and that instructions are current.

cards.title: Skills
cards.body: Packages of instructions and resources Claude loads when relevant — standard formats, team methods, recurring workflows. Create one with /skill-creator.
cards.note: Remember: a skill improves the workflow — it doesn't make the output automatically correct or approved.

cards.title: Artifacts
cards.body: Standalone outputs — documents, diagrams, visualisations, code snippets, simple web pages, interactive components. For a steering-group update, an artifact might be a milestone timeline, a process flow diagram, or a risk heatmap.
cards.note: Treat as a draft until checked against the source and Sandvik policy.

governance.intro: What's allowed, what needs care, and where final policy is still being confirmed. Where you see a placeholder, the local rule has not been finalised.

rows.title: Approved use
rows.body: Claude Chat is a Sandvik-approved tool for the conversational work described in this module — thinking, drafting, analysing, summarising and creating reusable outputs.

rows.title: Sensitive data
rows.body: Only enter information you are authorised to use. Protect personal, confidential and export-controlled material. Placeholder: confirm Sandvik data-classification rules for this tool.

rows.title: Connectors & permissions
rows.body: Use only Sandvik-approved connectors; they act through your login and permissions. The Microsoft 365 connector is pending approval. Pause before any action that sends, creates, updates or deletes in another system.

rows.title: Sharing or publishing
rows.body: Treat outputs as drafts. Before sharing, check what an artifact or download exposes, validate the information, and follow channel rules.

rows.title: Cost & usage limits
rows.body: Expect standard plan limits — five-hour session limits and weekly limits (Settings > Usage). Usage beyond the plan is billed pay-as-you-go to your cost center and can rise quickly. Need more capacity? Request a higher monthly limit via the intranet form — this requires cost-approver approval.

rows.body: Where to get help and report issues. Add the Sandvik intranet support link and contact route here.

scenario.title: Prepare a steering-group update
scenario.intro: Apply the workflow to a realistic Sandvik task — then run the review checklist before anything leaves your screen.
scenario.sourceMaterial: Approved internal docs: latest status report, the project risk log, and recent meeting notes.
scenario.goal: A one-page update plus a simple risk visualisation for next week's steering group.
toolActions: Open a Project and attach the approved documents as project knowledge.
Ask Claude to plan and make a checklist, then draft the update audience-first.
Request a risk-heatmap artifact summarising the risk log.
Optional: use an approved connector to pull the latest meeting transcript for action points.
reviewChecklist: Facts and figures verified against the source documents
Sensitive information removed or restricted appropriately
Artifact checked for what it exposes to the recipients
Assumptions flagged and the output cleared to share

risks.intro: Most problems fall into five groups. For each, there's a simple habit that avoids it.

groups.title: Data & confidentiality
groups.risk: Pasting information you're not cleared to use, giving connectors more access than needed, or trusting retrieved content that carries hidden instructions (prompt injection).
groups.doInstead: Enter only authorised material, prefer narrow access, and scan retrieved content before acting on it.

groups.title: Wrong tool choice
groups.risk: Forcing Claude Chat to do work that belongs in Claude Code, Cowork or Design — and getting weaker results.
groups.doInstead: Match the product to the work before you start.

groups.title: Over-trusting output
groups.risk: Treating a fluent answer as verified fact, trusting spreadsheet maths, or letting long, messy chats hide missed details.
groups.doInstead: Treat answers as drafts, verify important figures, and start a fresh focused chat when the topic changes.

groups.title: Sharing & publishing
groups.risk: Sharing artifacts or downloads without checking what they expose or validating the information first.
groups.doInstead: Run the review checklist before anything leaves your screen.

groups.title: Cost & usage
groups.risk: Long unfocused conversations, re-uploading the same files instead of using a project, or moving work to private accounts to dodge limits.
groups.doInstead: Scope context, reuse projects and artifacts, and request a higher limit through the proper route.

risks.footnote: Across all of these, one rule holds: human users remain accountable for outputs.

questions.prompt: A colleague needs Claude to read an existing Python repository, change several files, and run the tests. Which Claude product fits?

options.text: Claude Chat
options.feedback: Chat is for conversational work — drafting, analysis, Q&A. It doesn't read and change a codebase or run tests.

options.text: Claude Code
options.feedback: Correct. Reading and changing a codebase, running tests, and using dev tools belongs in Claude Code.

options.text: Claude Design
options.feedback: Design is for visual exploration, prototypes and slides.

options.text: Claude Cowork
options.feedback: Cowork suits multi-file desktop deliverables, but code work with tests belongs in Claude Code.

questions.explanation: Match the product to the work: Chat = conversation, Code = codebases, Cowork = multi-step desktop deliverables, Design = visuals.

questions.prompt: What does "agentic chat" mean in this module?

options.text: A separate agent you build once and reuse
options.feedback: That's a built agent — covered in the AI Champion Journey. Agentic chat is different.

options.text: Claude working through multiple steps inside the conversation, using approved context or tools, and continuing from what it finds
options.feedback: Correct. Not a separate agent — Claude plans, uses approved tools or context, and adapts within the chat.

options.text: Claude answering instantly with no steps
options.feedback: Agentic chat is precisely about working through steps.

options.text: A connector that runs automatically without you
options.feedback: You stay in control of whether tools are used.

questions.explanation: Agentic chat = user goal, approved tool use, returned context, Claude output, and human review — all inside the conversation.

questions.prompt: You ask Claude, through the Microsoft 365 connector, to summarise a SharePoint site you cannot open with your own account. What should you expect?

options.text: Claude reads it anyway — connectors have elevated access
options.feedback: Connectors do not bypass your permissions.

options.text: The connector acts through your login and permissions, so it cannot reach anything you can't reach yourself
options.feedback: Correct. If you can't access it in the source system, the connector can't either.

options.text: Claude will guess the likely contents
options.feedback: Claude should not invent content it cannot access.

questions.explanation: Connectors use your own login and permissions — they extend reach to what you're already allowed to see.

questions.prompt: You upload a 200-row budget spreadsheet and ask Claude for the column totals to drop into a report. What's the right habit?

options.text: Trust the totals — Claude is precise with numbers
options.feedback: Treat Claude as a reasoning and explanation aid, not a calculation engine.

options.text: Treat Claude as a reasoning aid and verify important calculations against the source file or a proper analysis tool
options.feedback: Correct. Inspect and explain with Claude, but check figures, formulas and row counts at the source.

options.text: Upload the whole finance system so Claude has more context
options.feedback: More context isn't always better — large, messy uploads raise the risk of confident mistakes.

questions.explanation: For data work, Claude helps summarise and explain — important numbers still need verification.

questions.prompt: Claude produces a risk-heatmap artifact for a steering-group update. Before you share it outside your team, you should:

options.text: Share it immediately — artifacts are finished outputs
options.feedback: Treat artifacts as drafts until they've been checked.

options.text: Check it doesn't expose sensitive information, validate the content against the source, and treat it as a draft until verified
options.feedback: Correct. Check exposure, validate the information, and confirm it's cleared to share.

options.text: Only check that the colours look right
options.feedback: Appearance isn't the risk — exposed information and unverified content are.

questions.explanation: Before sharing any artifact or download: check what it exposes, validate the information, and follow sharing rules.

questions.prompt: You keep hitting session limits doing legitimate business work in Claude. What's the correct action?

options.text: Move the work to your private Claude account to avoid limits
options.feedback: Never move Sandvik work into private or unapproved accounts.

options.text: Request a higher monthly usage / spending limit via the intranet form, expecting cost-approver approval
options.feedback: Correct. Request more capacity through the proper route; overage is billed pay-as-you-go to your cost center.

options.text: Create extra accounts to spread the usage
options.feedback: Using extra or private accounts to dodge limits is not allowed.

questions.explanation: Stay within approved tooling: wait for the reset, or request a higher limit (with cost-approver approval) via the intranet form.

completion.recap: Choose Chat for the right kind of work, give clear context and boundaries, use the context features deliberately, manage usage and cost, treat artifacts as drafts, verify important outputs, and follow Sandvik policy before sharing or relying on a result.
